questions: How many crystals, cleaves and fields of view did you measure, and how many showed the zero-bias-peak clusters and the 1T-layer gap?
Why were other fields of view or crystals set aside, and how were the "more than one hundred typical" spectra in Fig. 2d chosen from the roughly four thousand clusters in Fig. 2a?

Which ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown, for example temperature series on clusters other than the one at ε = -76 meV in Fig. 3h, and the field range and direction behind Supplementary Fig. 10?
What does the second-best dataset look like, for example Fig. 2d or Fig. 4e rebuilt from a second crystal or from the other STM system?

Were the widths in Figs. 3f and 3h corrected for thermal smearing (about 1.3 meV full width at 4.2 K) and for the lock-in modulation? The plotted HWHM runs from about 0.65 to 1.7 meV against about 2.4 meV for the Kondo line, a factor of about 1.5 to 4, so could you say how "an order of magnitude" follows, and which parameters set the gray line?

Which hybridization scale enters your T_K estimate? The formula uses the narrow-band width W0; how does T_K change if the 1T-1H hybridization is used, and could it fall into the 0.3 to 4.2 K window of Fig. 3h?

Did the spectrum of a given cluster change with setpoint bias, current or tip height? In 4Hb-TaS2 the tip has been reported to toggle clusters between a Kondo cluster state and a flat-band state, with hysteresis.

How exactly were the spectra in Fig. 2d normalized, do the trends in Figs. 3d and 3e hold in the raw spectra, and why are the fits Lorentzian in Fig. 3b and Fano for Fig. 3f? (The text cites "Fig. 3g" for the spectral weight, which the caption labels 3e.)
